spatial_claims.claim: A lies on lesser circle gamma, so OA = r, and A is inside greater circle Gamma
OA produced meets Gamma at E, so E is on Gamma with OE = R
Through A, perpendicular to OE meets Gamma at B and C; A lies between B and C on chord BC
OA is perpendicular to BC, so A is foot of perpendicular from O to chord BC
Two perpendicular diameters through O divide Gamma into four sectors with 90-degree central angles
Repeated quartering of central angles yields common angle alpha < theta (angle BOC)
All polygon vertices lie on Gamma; polygon has 4 times 4^n sides (even); all sides subtend equal central angle alpha
Each triangle formed by O and two adjacent vertices has equal radial sides and equal included angle, so polygon is equilateral
In triangles OBC and OUV: OB = OU = OC = OV = R (radii), angle BOC = theta > alpha = angle UOV, therefore BC > UV by I.24
OH is perpendicular distance from O to chord UV; since BC > UV, BC is nearer center (III.15), so OH > OA = r
Every point X on line UV satisfies OX >= OH > r, so every point on each side of polygon is at distance > r from O
Every point on gamma is at distance exactly r from O, so no side of polygon touches gamma

configuration_map: O is the common center of concentric circles Gamma (radius R) and gamma (radius r), with R > r. Point A lies on gamma along a radius, with E the intersection of that radius with Gamma. Chord BC of Gamma passes through A perpendicular to OE, making A the foot of the perpendicular from O to BC, so the perpendicular distance from O to BC equals OA = r. Two perpendicular diameters through O create four 90-degree sectors, which are repeatedly quartered until the common central angle alpha is less than theta (angle BOC). The resulting polygon vertices on Gamma are equally spaced by angle alpha. For any side UV of the polygon, the perpendicular distance OH from O to UV exceeds r because UV is a shorter chord than BC (by I.24 and the angle inequality), and shorter chords in a circle are farther from the center (by III.15). Every point on each side is therefore farther than r from O, so no side meets gamma.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The key geometric chain is sound: A is simultaneously on gamma and is the foot of the perpendicular from O to chord BC, so the perpendicular distance from O to BC equals r. The angle comparison (theta > alpha) correctly yields BC > UV via I.24, and the chord-distance theorem III.15 correctly yields OH > OA = r. The right-triangle argument in Step 7 correctly extends the distance inequality to all points on each side. No contradictions exist between any pair of spatial claims across steps.
